questions.question: In a row of boys, Rahul is 33rd from the left end. Rajat is 17 ranks to the right of Rahul. If Rajat is 35th from right end, then what will be the rank of Rahul from the right end?
questions.solution:
Rahul’s rank from the left = 33

Rajat’s rank from the right = 35

Rajat’s rank = 17 to the right of Rahul

So, Rajat’s rank from the left = 33 + 17

→ 50

Total students = Rajat’s rank from left + Rajat’s rank from the right – 1

→ 50 + 35 – 1

→ 84

Rahul’s rank from the right = Total students – Rahul’s rank from the left – 1

→ 84 – 33 + 1 = 52

Hence, Rahul’s rank from the right is 52.

questions.solution:
The shopkeeper increases the list price of his product by 20% and then provide 20% discount on the list price.

By formula:

Profit/Loss % = [(% increase in price) × (% decrease in price)] ÷ 100 

= [(+20) × (-20)] ÷ 100 ('+' sign is used to denote increase in price and '-' sign is used to denote discount)

= -400 ÷ 100

= -4%

The negative sign here implies that loss is made.

Therefore, the shopkeeper makes a loss of 4% on the product.

Hence, ‘**4% loss**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: By which Constitutional Amendment Act the eleventh fundamental duty was added to the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86th Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, added the eleventh fundamental duty to the Indian Constitution under Article 51A.
 
• This amendment emphasizes the duty of every citizen to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the ages of 6 and 14 years.
 
• It was introduced alongside the insertion of Article 21A, which made education a fundamental right for children in the specified age group.
 
• The eleventh fundamental duty was added to ensure active participation in the realization of the Right to Education (RTE).
 
• The amendment aligns with the Directive Principles of State Policy and aims to promote inclusive education across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 51A - Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Fundamental duties were added to the Constitution of India by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, under the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, there were 10 fundamental duties listed under Article 51A.
 
• The 86th Amendment Act, 2002, added the eleventh duty related to education.
 
• Fundamental duties are non-justiciable, meaning citizens cannot be legally compelled to perform them.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (Article 21A)**
 
 
• Article 21A was introduced by the 86th Amendment Act, making free and compulsory education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It mandates the state to provide education to all children in this age group.
 
• The Right to Education Act, 2009, was enacted to operationalize this provision.
 
• This initiative aims to reduce illiteracy and empower children through education.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**
 
 
• DPSPs are guidelines for the government to establish a social order based on justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• Article 45 of the DPSP initially stated that the State should provide free and compulsory education for children up to the age of 14 years.
 
• Article 21A and the eleventh fundamental duty are direct advancements of this directive.
 
• These principles are not enforceable by law but serve as a framework for policymaking.
 
 
 
• **Education Initiatives by Indian Government**
 
 
• Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan integrates various schemes like SSA, RMSA, and Teacher Education to improve school education.
 
• Mid-Day Meal Scheme provides nutritional support to children and encourages school attendance.
 
• Digital initiatives like DIKSHA aim to leverage technology for enhancing education quality.
 
• Programs like Beti Bachao Beti Padhao promote education among girls to address gender disparity.

__
 
• **Discovery of similar pottery styles:**

 
 
• Archaeologists have found similar pottery styles across various Harappan sites.
 
• This suggests a shared cultural framework among different regions of the Harappan civilization.
 
 
 
• **Reason for similarity:**
 
 
• Pottery was traded between Harappan cities, leading to homogeneity in material culture.
 
• This trade facilitated the spread of similar styles and techniques across different regions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** list of different types of **pottery found in ancient India**:

 
• 
 
**Black and Red Ware (BRW)**: Characterized by a black interior and red exterior, this pottery was common during the Harappan and early Vedic periods.

 
 
• 
 
**Painted Grey Ware (PGW)**: Associated with the late Vedic period, PGW features simple painted geometric patterns, often in black or deep red.

 
 
• 
 
**Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW)**: A highly polished, glossy black pottery that flourished during the Mauryan period (circa 700-200 BCE).

 
 
• 
 
**Ochre-Colored Pottery (OCP)**: Dating back to the late Harappan and Chalcolithic periods, this pottery is ochre in color and found mainly in the Indo-Gangetic plains.

 
 
• 
 
**Grey Ware**: Used during the Iron Age, especially by the later Vedic civilization, often found in regions like Uttar Pradesh and Haryana.

 
 
• 
 
**Red Ware**: Common across multiple periods, red ware pottery was made of coarse clay and typically unpainted, used from the Harappan period to early historic times.

 
 
• 
 
**Black Slipped Ware (BSW)**: A fine, well-polished black pottery, found in different regions, often associated with the Later Harappan and Vedic periods.

 
 
• 
 
**Jorwe Ware**: Found in the Chalcolithic Jorwe culture of Maharashtra, this pottery is red or buff-colored with painted designs.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasty built the famous Ellora caves?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ellora Caves were primarily patronized and constructed under the **Rashtrakuta dynasty**, particularly during the 8th to 10th centuries CE.
 
• The most famous structure in the Ellora Caves is the **Kailasa Temple (Cave 16)**, an architectural marvel carved entirely out of a single rock.
 
• The Rashtrakutas were known for their **artistic and architectural contributions**, and Ellora is a testament to their grandeur and engineering skills.
 
• The Ellora complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and comprises **34 rock-cut caves**, including Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain monuments.
 
• Ellora symbolized **religious harmony** and cultural diversity, as its monuments represent the coexistence of Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ellora Caves Overview:**

 
 
• Located in the Chatrapati Sambhaji Nagar district of Maharashtra, India, Ellora is one of the largest rock-cut monastery-temple complexes in the world.
 
• It features **12 Buddhist caves** (caves 1–12), **17 Hindu caves** (caves 13–29), and **5 Jain caves** (caves 30–34).
 
• The caves were excavated between the 6th and 10th centuries CE.
 
• They showcase intricate sculptures, paintings, and architectural brilliance.
 
 
 
• **Kailasa Temple (Cave 16):**
 
 
• It is the largest monolithic structure in the world, dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
• The temple was commissioned by the Rashtrakuta king **Krishna I** in the 8th century CE.
 
• The temple mimics Mount Kailash, the mythical abode of Lord Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Rashtrakutas ruled large parts of India between the 6th and 10th centuries CE.
 
• They were known for their patronage of art, culture, and architecture.
 
• Other notable contributions include the Kannada classic Kavirajamarga and the Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status:**
 
 
• The Ellora Caves were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
 
• They are recognized for their outstanding universal value and architectural significance.

 Moving coil meter

questions.question: If x+(1)/(x)=sqrt{13}, then one of the values x³-(1)/(x³) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If x + 1/x = k, then x − 1/x = √(k² − 4).

Here, k = √13, so x − 1/x = √(13 − 4) = √9 = 3.

If x − 1/x = a, then x³ − 1/x³ = a³ + 3a.

Substituting a = 3, we get: 3³ + 3 × 3 = 27 + 9 = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + 1/x = √13

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab

a³ − b³ = (a − b)³ + 3ab(a − b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = (x + 1/x)² − 4(x)(1/x)

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = (√13)² − 4

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = 13 − 4 = 9

⇒ x − 1/x = ±3

Taking x − 1/x = 3 (since the positive value matches the given options):

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = (x − 1/x)³ + 3(x)(1/x)(x − 1/x)

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 3³ + 3 × 3

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 27 + 9 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2. This is derived directly from expanding the whole square formula (x + 1/x)².

Difference of Squares Transition

The relationship between the sum and difference of reciprocal terms is given by the identity (x + 1/x)² − (x − 1/x)² = 4.

Sum of Cubes Identity

If x + 1/x = k, then x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k. This comes from rearranging the expansion of (x + 1/x)³.

Difference of Cubes Identity

If x − 1/x = k, then x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k. This is an essential shortcut for quickly solving differences of cubed terms in algebra.
</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is two-third of its total surface area. If the total surface area is 231 cm², then its volume is:

Ratio of CSA to TSA = h : (r + h) = 2 : 3 ⇒ h = 2r.

Given TSA = 6πr² = 231 ⇒ r² = 231 × 7 ÷ (6 × 22) = 49/4 ⇒ r = 7/2 cm.

Height h = 2 × (7/2) = 7 cm.

Volume = πr²h = (22/7) × (49/4) × 7 = 269.5 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 269.5 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 231 cm²

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2/3 of TSA

**Formula Used:**

TSA = 2πr(r + h)

CSA = 2πrh

Volume = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3fd255cc607c0f1a15fbd172752da12aad944485ab1047f76ce07e2274a6ce31.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CSA = (2/3) × 231 = 154 cm²

⇒ We know that, TSA = CSA + 2 × Area of Base

⇒ 231 = 154 + 2πr²

⇒ 2πr² = 231 − 154 = 77

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r² = 77

⇒ (44/7) × r² = 77

⇒ r² = (77 × 7) ÷ 44 = 49/4

⇒ r = 7/2 = 3.5 cm

⇒ Now, substitute r in the CSA formula:

⇒ 2πrh = 154

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × (7/2) × h = 154

⇒ 22 × h = 154

⇒ h = 154 ÷ 22 = 7 cm

⇒ Volume of cylinder = πr²h

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (7/2) × (7/2) × 7

⇒ Volume = 11 × 7 × 7 ÷ 2 = 539 ÷ 2 = 269.5 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 269.5 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cylinder Surface Areas

The Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder is 2πrh. The Total Surface Area (TSA) includes the two circular bases, calculated as 2πr(r + h).

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume represents the total 3D space enclosed and is given by πr²h, where r is the base radius and h is the height.

Relation to a Cone

A cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder has exactly one-third the volume of the cylinder (Volume = 1/3 × πr²h).

questions.question: The external radius and internal radius of a hollow cylinder are 42 cm and 36 cm and its length is 56 cm. If we put two hollow cones of a height of 28 cm one on the top and one on the bottom then what will be the volume of the material used to make the structure? Given the external and internal radius of the cone is the same as the cylinder.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the volume formulas for both the cylinder and cones involve π (≈ ²²⁄₇), the total final volume must be a multiple of 11.

We can quickly use the divisibility rule of 11 (difference between the sum of alternating digits) on the given options:

⇒ 108924 → (1 + 8 + 2) − (0 + 9 + 4) = 11 − 13 = −2 (Not divisible)

⇒ 109856 → (1 + 9 + 5) − (0 + 8 + 6) = 15 − 14 = 1 (Not divisible)

⇒ 109824 → (1 + 9 + 2) − (0 + 8 + 4) = 12 − 12 = 0 (Divisible by 11)

Only 109824 is perfectly divisible by 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 109824 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ External radius (R) = 42 cm

⇒ Internal radius (r) = 36 cm

⇒ Height of the hollow cylinder (H) = 56 cm

⇒ Height of each hollow cone (h) = 28 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Volume of hollow cylinder = π(R² − r²)H

⇒ Volume of a hollow cone = ¹⁄₃ × π(R² − r²)h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total material volume = Volume of hollow cylinder + (2 × Volume of hollow cone)

⇒ Total volume = π(R² − r²)H + 2 × [ ¹⁄₃ × π(R² − r²)h ]

⇒ Total volume = π(R² − r²) × [ H + ²h⁄₃ ]

⇒ R² − r² = 42² − 36²

⇒ R² − r² = (42 + 36) × (42 − 36) = 78 × 6 = 468 cm²

⇒ Total volume = ²²⁄₇ × 468 × [ 56 + (2 × 28) ÷ 3 ]

⇒ Total volume = ²²⁄₇ × 468 × [ 56 + ⁵⁶⁄₃ ]

⇒ Total volume = ²²⁄₇ × 468 × [ ²²⁴⁄₃ ]

⇒ Total volume = 22 × (468 ÷ 3) × (224 ÷ 7)

⇒ Total volume = 22 × 156 × 32

⇒ Total volume = 109824 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 109824 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Hollow Cylinder

The volume of material used in a hollow cylindrical tube is given by V = π(R² − r²)H. It essentially subtracts the empty inner volume from the total outer volume.

Divisibility Rule of 11 in Geometry

In mensuration problems involving circular cross-sections (spheres, cones, cylinders), the final resulting quantity will frequently be a multiple of 11 due to the involvement of π (≈ ²²⁄₇). Leveraging this allows for rapid elimination of options without calculating the final product.

The Total Surface Area involves the outer curved surface, the inner curved surface, and the two top/bottom circular rings: TSA = 2πRH + 2πrH + 2π(R² − r²).

questions.question: The speed of the stream is 4 km/h. A boat can cover a distance of 40 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 4 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water (in km/h).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For such quadratic equation problems, checking the options is the fastest method.

Total time = [Downstream distance ÷ (v + u)] + [Upstream distance ÷ (v − u)]

⇒ 40 / (v + 4) + 12 / (v − 4) = 4

⇒ 10 / (v + 4) + 3 / (v − 4) = 1

Checking Option 4: Put v = 12 ⇒ 10 / 16 + 3 / 8 = 5 / 8 + 3 / 8 = 1. (Condition is satisfied)

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/34db17e5fb2fd183ab0b9d50db5b135d29ea68260e6b409017b6ef61287bca3a.png] 

**Given:**

Speed of stream (u) = 4 km/h

Downstream distance = 40 km

Upstream distance = 12 km

Total Time = 4 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water (v) + Speed of stream (u)

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water (v) − Speed of stream (u)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Time = (40 ÷ (v + 4)) + (12 ÷ (v − 4))

⇒ 4 = 40 / (v + 4) + 12 / (v − 4)

Dividing the entire equation by 4:

⇒ 10 / (v + 4) + 3 / (v − 4) = 1

⇒ [10(v − 4) + 3(v + 4)] ÷ [(v + 4)(v − 4)] = 1

⇒ 10v − 40 + 3v + 12 = v² − 16

⇒ 13v − 28 = v² − 16

⇒ v² − 13v + 12 = 0

⇒ v² − 12v − v + 12 = 0

⇒ v(v − 12) − 1(v − 12) = 0

⇒ (v − 12)(v − 1) = 0

Thus, v = 12 or v = 1.

Since the boat is able to travel upstream against a 4 km/h stream, its speed must be greater than the stream speed (v > 4).

⇒ v = 12 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat and Stream

If downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, then Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Current

The velocity of the current or stream can be calculated as = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Equal Distance

When a boat travels equal distances upstream and downstream, the Average Speed over the entire journey = (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

Multiplying factor for 4% growth = 1 + (4/100) = 104/100 = 26/25.

**Given:**

Projected population in 2030 (A) = 1,58,18,400

Growth rate (R) = 4% per decade

Time period (n) = (2030 − 2000) ÷ 10 = 3 decades

**Formula Used:**

A = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

Where A is the final population, P is the initial population, R is the rate of growth, and n is the time period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78596e327b475a56e35988dc5f6f4a73c1e95ca6909d262dc895297106490b1f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1,58,18,400 = P × (1 + 4/100)³

⇒ 1,58,18,400 = P × (104/100)³

⇒ 1,58,18,400 = P × (26/25)³

⇒ P = 1,58,18,400 × (25/26) × (25/26) × (25/26)

⇒ P = 1,58,18,400 × (15625 / 17576)

⇒ P = 900 × 15625

⇒ P = 1,40,62,500

Compound Population Growth

When a population grows at a constant rate R over a certain period, it increases exponentially in a manner identical to compound interest. The standard formula applied is Final Population = Initial Population × (1 + R/100)ⁿ.

Population Depreciation

If the population decreases consistently by a certain percentage R over a period (such as due to mortality or migration), the decay formula becomes Final Population = Initial Population × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.

Successive Percentage Change

When the population grows or shrinks at varying rates (R₁%, R₂%, R₃%) in successive time periods, the net final population is calculated as P × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100) × (1 ± R₃/100).

questions.question: Two trains started at the same time, one from A to B and other from B to A. They arrive at B and A respectively in 2 hours and 8 hours after they pass each other, what is the ratio of speeds of the two trains?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects move towards each other and take t₁ and t₂ hours to reach their destinations after crossing:

Speed Ratio (S₁ : S₂) = √(t₂ ÷ t₁)

Given, t₁ = 2 hours and t₂ = 8 hours.

Speed Ratio = √(8 ÷ 2) = √4 = 2 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Train 1 to reach B after meeting, t₁ = 2 hours.

Time taken by Train 2 to reach A after meeting, t₂ = 8 hours.

**Formula Used:**

If two trains start simultaneously from points A and B towards each other and after crossing take t₁ and t₂ time to reach their respective destinations, then:

S₁ ÷ S₂ = √(t₂ ÷ t₁)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/907fa39c56bbed2e424b6e0f314d2c0e3ce2681fb177f7e81bd88cbfdbd1b446.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ S₁ ÷ S₂ = √(8 ÷ 2)

⇒ S₁ ÷ S₂ = √4

⇒ S₁ ÷ S₂ = 2 ÷ 1

⇒ S₁ : S₂ = 2 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Point Distance Ratio

When two objects start at the same time, the distance traveled by them until they meet is directly proportional to their speeds (D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂).

Total Time to Meet

If they take t₁ and t₂ times to reach their respective destinations after meeting, the total time taken to meet is given by t = √(t₁ × t₂).

Relative Speed

For objects moving in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂. For objects moving in the same direction, it is S₁ − S₂.
</p
